goal_title: Book: Wavefunctions: What Returns — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in wavefunctions became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

reading.arc: The sequence opens by splitting a returning position from a returning state: the bob threads the same ring twice with opposite signs, and a number (the crossing count) keeps something the eye cannot. It then gives the swing a record that occupies space (time as depth, three sampling policies with two endings), lets one sine rule become terrain a body collides with and a passage that only suggests, and only then shows where sine comes from, as the projection of a turning point. The second half moves outward: a lattice where a disturbance travels while its parts stay home, one oscillation inside another's phase, a rhythm kept in a column, chance inside a prepared vocabulary, a struck voice that outlives the hand, a sampled helix that still needs provision for a body, a beat that belongs to a relationship rather than a third source. It closes by adding sines on purpose at a bench whose recipe labels have a tolerance, detours into a room that feeds each return into the next, and hands Randomness the question of what must be retained to bring a result back.
holds: A readout that keeps what the eye cannot, and prose that asks what the readout leaves out: crossings and signed omega (Intro), actual gaps and step (Pendulum), STILL IN at a deadline (tray), x-gap measured one way (corridor), neighbour peak in mm (lattice), differs: (FM rig), voices and ages (metallophone), sum against total (bench).

A chosen beginning, never a first one: the counter already above zero, RESET that resets the experiment and not the room, BASELINE as a reference rather than a sound before all decisions, a seed in the next sequence.
One line of sin() shown each time it takes a new job: restoring force, depth from age, tray height, wall displacement, phase inside a carrier, a voice under a decay, a coefficient in a sum.

A direction given another job: time as depth (Pendulum), time as an angle on a drum (seismograph), a turn read through height (Bernini), angle as height on a stair (Sky Stairs), a slow envelope from two fast motions (beat).

The body as receiver: what a wave holds (tray), what it permits without collision (corridor), what a sampled curve needs before a body can use it (Sky Stairs) — the sequence's truth that a returning value is not the same as a returning state.
Forward handovers that name the next hall's device, so each closing paragraph is a small promise the next room keeps (with one exception, Effect Sound).

hall_notes.note: Opens on the ring the bob keeps leaving; the signed velocity readout and the crossing counter split position from state, the four-line physics step and the release dot product are quoted exactly, and it leaves wanting more than a number. Reads cleanly; every quoted line is used.

Time becomes depth at 0.6 m per second; FINE, COARSE and STROBE are three sampling policies with two endings written into the list; RESET begins without beginning everything. Reads well; the one heavy ask is counting FINE marks (about 118 per swing).

Two encounters: a colliding sine tray (32 bodies, a 12 s window, SIZE and RELIEF) and a corridor of collision-less walls with AMP, PHASE, FREEZE and an x-gap that stays 2.00 m because of how it is measured. Long but earned; compass words and one RELIEF sentence are the soft spots.

The hinge: sine and cosine as the two projections of one turning point, a beginning chosen to label a cycle that has none, a height that does not recover the angle. Precise prose written for a moving point that the code stops after two cycles.

Follow one sphere, then a pair, then the same push with and without links; a neighbour-peak readout in millimetres and an edge that is part of the mechanism. Careful and a little abstract; the chapter's verbs (select PULSE) do not match the panel's captions.

BASELINE, HOLD, PLAY and COMPARE make a phase-modulation rig into an ear experiment; the output line, the modulator envelope, the 0.3 s retrigger and the scope's divided lane all check against the source. Opens without locating the rig in a crowded hall; the outro skips Cage.

Two changes to disentangle: a twist built into the profile and a slow whole-object rotation; circular coordinates now place solid matter. Short and clear; silent about the vowel board repeating a phrase in the same hall.

A listening protocol rather than a control: continuous layer against intermittent events, vocabulary against sequence, chance inside a frame. Honest about the title; reads as instructions for attention, which suits a work with no hand controls.

The best-grounded chapter: strike, restrike, pair, stick return, the 7.5 s buffer and the 12 ms ribbon all trace to code, and 'length chosen from the note' is the sequence's clearest reversal. One phrase ('final tenth') misreads the fade.

A sampled helix whose radius breathes (0.45 m in the scene), membranes that admit the gaps, and the distinction between positions and a route. Reads as an inspection from the floor, which is what the map affords; one author's status line leaks into the prose.
A, B and A+B rows, the sum drawn at half height, a readout of |fA - fB|, visual only. Clear and true; it never mentions the walking path the hall is named for.

The bench (five sliders, HOLD, BASELINE, H1 ALONE, the amber mark, a recipe classifier with a 0.025 tolerance) then a second work under its own H2, the Lucier room, with two footnotes, and a three-sentence return. Rich and code-true, but the detour outweighs the primary and the coda is thin.

stumbles: WaveFunctions_Unit_Circle: the point and its rods stop after two cycles (about 16 s after the hall is built) with no restart, so the visitor meets a frozen figure while the chapter says 'Follow the point' and Sine_Space's outro promised 'a graph grows beside it'.
WaveFunctions_Pendulum: 'Count the marks between them' is asked under FINE, where a swing holds about 118 marks; COARSE (about fifteen) is introduced a paragraph later.

WaveFunctions_3D_Wave_Propagation: 'select PULSE' and 'Change COUPLED to INDEPENDENT' name states, not buttons; the buttons are DRIVE and COUPLING and their captions show the current state, so PULSE is not on the panel until SINE is pressed.
Wavefunctions_Bernini: a vowel board repeats 'right here, right now' every three seconds; the chapter's 'accompanying generated sound' leaves the visitor to hear the columns speaking.
Wavefunctions_Sky_Stairs: 'This room still needs that full walking check.' is a production note in reader prose; a headset visitor cannot perform it.
WaveFunctions_Effect_Sound: no locating sentence for the rig among 28 works, and the outro puts AirMusic straight after Bernini when Cage stands between.
WaveFunctions_Synthesis_Lab: 'Take this short detour' is a scene change out of the hall and back, some 750 words long, followed by three sentences at the bench.
WaveFunctions_Sine_Space (also Pendulum, Synthesis_Lab): 'west mouth', 'west nook', 'west walkway', 'north wall' — these maps define no spawn (sp is a score cube) and a headset shows no compass.
WaveFunctions_AirMusic: 'a short fade in its final tenth' reads as the last 0.75 s of the buffer; the code eases the last 0.1 s.
WaveFunctions_Sine_Space: 'This control raises the difference' — from the shipped middle relief the second RELIEF press lowers it.

keep.quote: The body can be still for an instant without having finished moving.
We can walk beside a duration because a direction has been given another job.
This can become an instrument for finding repetition. It can also make repetition look like stillness.
We have made a constant width by deciding how to measure it. Which width would matter to a body trying to get through?
A beginning is needed to label the progression, even though the circle itself has no privileged first point.
The rig reports changed parameters, but there is no field in its list for the difference that made you want to listen again.
The length is chosen from the note, not the note from the length
Something has left the picture without leaving the calculation.

reading.handover_in: FormFinding_Forge closes with 'The next sequence begins with oscillation. A form can persist through returning motion as well as through rest; settling is only one way for a system to continue.' and Intro opens on the ring the bob keeps leaving; Intro's 'We have met position, velocity and force in earlier rooms' acknowledges the road in. Clean, nothing to fix.
reading.handover_out: Synthesis_Lab ends by naming Random_Definition and its question (what must we retain to bring an unfamiliar result back?), and Random_Definition opens 'In Synthesis Lab, five amounts could bring a familiar curve back.' A tight pair. Its only weakness is placement: the bench's distinction between repeating a recipe and repeating an instant arrives in three sentences after the long Lucier detour.

tasks.title: Keep the point turning after the bridge completes, or write for the finished figure
tasks.spec:
[encounter] WaveFunctions_Unit_Circle
Quote: “Follow the point on the circle and look at the projection rods beside it. When the point reaches the top, compare its height with the corresponding part of the wave.”
Why: The figure freezes about 16 s after the hall is built and has no restart, so almost every visitor meets a still point and a finished graph; the chapter's hedge ('If the drawing has already finished') is the normal case, and Sine_Space's outro promised a graph that grows. If the freeze is wanted instead, open the chapter on the finished figure, turn the four-position exercise into reading the completed steps, and soften Sine_Space's 'a graph grows beside it'.

tasks.title: The fade is the last tenth of a second
tasks.spec:
[code-claim] WaveFunctions_AirMusic
